items.title: Summary lists each bag line with name, quantity and line total
covers: AC1: Order summary section lists each bag line with product name, quantity and line total
items.reason: AC1 is the core of the story: the shopper must see each bag line with name, quantity and line total before ordering. A wrong multiplication (unit price instead of unit price × quantity) or a missing line would mislead the shopper. Only the rendered checkout page shows this, so the case runs e2e.

items.title: Summary lines follow the shopping bag's order
covers: AC1: lines in the same order as the shopping bag
items.reason: AC1 requires the summary to list lines "in the same order as the shopping bag". In TC-SUMM-1-01 the bag order coincides with catalog id order, so a summary sorted by product id or name would still pass; this case adds the harness first so only true bag order passes. It needs the real bag and both pages, hence e2e.

items.title: Summary shows the item count 3 and order total $309.97
items.reason: AC2 requires the item count (sum of quantities, not number of lines) and the order total. Counting lines would show 2 instead of 3, which is the likely bug; the total must be the sum of line totals. Kept separate from TC-SUMM-1-01 because it checks the totals block, not the lines.

items.title: Line total and order total above $1,000 use the bag's thousands format
covers: AC2: formatted like the shopping bag's prices
items.reason: AC2 says amounts are "formatted like the shopping bag's prices". Below $1,000 almost any two-decimal format matches, so the boundary that tells formats apart is the thousands separator: the bag shows `$1,099.90`, formatted with N2 in the invariant culture. A summary using a different format, such as F2 or a culture-specific one, would drop the comma and show the digits 1099.90 instead. Comparing against the bag page's own text on the same bag pins "like the shopping bag".

items.title: Changing a quantity in the bag updates the summary on the next checkout visit
covers: AC3: new quantity, line total and order total after a bag change
items.reason: AC3 protects against a stale summary (cached bag, or totals computed once). The shopper must see the committed new quantity, line total, item count and order total when returning to checkout. It spans the bag page and two checkout loads, so it runs e2e.

items.title: Empty bag shows "Your shopping bag is empty" instead of list and totals
covers: AC4: summary says "Your shopping bag is empty" instead of the list and totals
items.reason: AC4 defines the empty state: a message replaces the list and the totals. Rendering an empty list with `Items 0` / `Total $0.00` would violate it. Alice's seeded basket is empty, so no setup beyond signing in is needed.

items.title: Place order with an empty bag still shows "Your cart is empty"
covers: AC4: pressing Place order still shows "Your cart is empty"
items.reason: AC4 requires the existing empty-cart guard to keep working: the new summary text must not replace or bypass the "Your cart is empty" validation, and no order may be created. The risk is a regression in the form submit path after `OnInitialized` became `OnInitializedAsync`. Checking the orders page proves nothing was placed.

items.title: Summary shows only the signed-in shopper's bag, not another user's
covers: AC1: summary lists her (the signed-in shopper's) bag lines
items.reason: AC1 says the summary lists "her shopping bag". Leaking another user's bag into the summary (wrong buyer id, shared cache in the server-rendered page) would show private data and wrong totals. Two separate browser contexts on the test stack are the only realistic way to check this.

items.title: Placing the order from checkout lands on the orders page with the new order
covers: AC5: the order is placed and she lands on her orders
items.reason: AC5 requires that adding the summary (and loading the bag in `OnInitializedAsync`) does not break placing an order. The risk is the submit postback failing or not navigating. The order travels WebApp → Basket → event bus → Ordering, so only the full test stack proves it.

items.title: Shipping address validation still blocks an order with an empty Address
covers: AC5: the shipping address form and its validation are unchanged
items.reason: AC5 requires the shipping address validation to be unchanged. The `EditContext` is now built inside `OnInitializedAsync`; if it were rebuilt or bound wrongly the `[Required]` rule on Street could stop firing and an order with no address would be placed. Uses a non-empty bag so the only reason to refuse is the address.

items.title: "Back to the shopping bag" link still returns to /cart
covers: AC5: the "Back to the shopping bag" link is unchanged
items.reason: AC5 names the back link as unchanged. Moving markup to fit the summary could drop or retarget it. A single click on the rendered page is the cheapest proof.
